title: 2 Kings 12: Repairing the House and Dealing Faithfully
body:
Read the chapter → [2 Kings 12](/bible/2-kings/12)

**[2 Kings 12:1-3](/bible/2-kings/12#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/2-kings/12#v1)</sup> In the seventh year of Jehu Jehoash began to reign; and forty years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Zibiah of Beer–sheba.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/2-kings/12#v2)</sup> And Jehoash did that which was right in the sight of the Lord all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/2-kings/12#v3)</sup> But the high places were not taken away: the people still sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.

- Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu and reigned forty years in Jerusalem.
- He did that which was right in the sight of the Most High all the days that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
- No one comes to the truth alone; the Most High set up a structure of instruction, and a person must be taught the word rather than claiming private revelation.
  - **[Romans 10:13-15](/bible/romans/10#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/romans/10#v13)</sup> For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/romans/10#v14)</sup> How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/romans/10#v15)</sup> And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!

    None can call on the Lord unless they believe, none believe unless they hear, and none hear without a preacher who is sent to guide and instruct.

**[2 Kings 12:4-8](/bible/2-kings/12#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/2-kings/12#v4)</sup> And Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the dedicated things that is brought into the house of the Lord, even the money of every one that passeth the account, the money that every man is set at, and all the money that cometh into any man’s heart to bring into the house of the Lord,
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/2-kings/12#v5)</sup> Let the priests take it to them, every man of his acquaintance: and let them repair the breaches of the house, wheresoever any breach shall be found.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/2-kings/12#v6)</sup> But it was so, that in the three and twentieth year of king Jehoash the priests had not repaired the breaches of the house.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/2-kings/12#v7)</sup> Then king Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest, and the other priests, and said unto them, Why repair ye not the breaches of the house? now therefore receive no more money of your acquaintance, but deliver it for the breaches of the house.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/2-kings/12#v8)</sup> And the priests consented to receive no more money of the people, neither to repair the breaches of the house.

- Jehoash ordered that all the dedicated money brought into the house be gathered by the priests to repair the breaches of the house.
- But by the twenty-third year of his reign the priests still had not repaired the breaches, though he had come to power around age seven.
- Jehoash called Jehoiada and the priests, asked why the house was not repaired, and directed that the money no longer be received by them but delivered directly for the repairs.

**[2 Kings 12:9-16](/bible/2-kings/12#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/2-kings/12#v9)</sup> But Jehoiada the priest took a chest, and bored a hole in the lid of it, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one cometh into the house of the Lord: and the priests that kept the door put therein all the money that was brought into the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/2-kings/12#v10)</sup> And it was so, when they saw that there was much money in the chest, that the king’s scribe and the high priest came up, and they put up in bags, and told the money that was found in the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/2-kings/12#v11)</sup> And they gave the money, being told, into the hands of them that did the work, that had the oversight of the house of the Lord: and they laid it out to the carpenters and builders, that wrought upon the house of the Lord,
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/2-kings/12#v12)</sup> And to masons, and hewers of stone, and to buy timber and hewed stone to repair the breaches of the house of the Lord, and for all that was laid out for the house to repair it.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/2-kings/12#v13)</sup> Howbeit there were not made for the house of the Lord bowls of silver, snuffers, basons, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that was brought into the house of the Lord:
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/2-kings/12#v14)</sup> But they gave that to the workmen, and repaired therewith the house of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/2-kings/12#v15)</sup> Moreover they reckoned not with the men, into whose hand they delivered the money to be bestowed on workmen: for they dealt faithfully.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/2-kings/12#v16)</sup> The trespass money and sin money was not brought into the house of the Lord: it was the priests’.

- Jehoiada took a chest, bored a hole in the lid, and set it beside the altar, and the priests put in all the money brought to the house.
- When there was much money, the king's scribe and the high priest counted it and gave it into the hands of the workmen who oversaw the repair.
- The money went to carpenters, builders, masons, and for timber and stone, and none was diverted to make vessels; the workmen dealt faithfully so no reckoning was needed.
- This is why records must be kept, especially where money is concerned; all things touching the body must be put in writing.
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 42:7](/bible/sirach/42#v7)**  Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.

**[2 Kings 12:17-21](/bible/2-kings/12#v17)**

> <sup>[17](/bible/2-kings/12#v17)</sup> Then Hazael king of Syria went up, and fought against Gath, and took it: and Hazael set his face to go up to Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/2-kings/12#v18)</sup> And Jehoash king of Judah took all the hallowed things that Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own hallowed things, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the house of the Lord, and in the king’s house, and sent it to Hazael king of Syria: and he went away from Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/2-kings/12#v19)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/2-kings/12#v20)</sup> And his servants arose, and made a conspiracy, and slew Joash in the house of Millo, which goeth down to Silla.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/2-kings/12#v21)</sup> For Jozachar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, smote him, and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David: and Amaziah his son reigned in his stead.

- Hazael king of Syria took Gath and set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
- Jehoash took the hallowed things dedicated by the former kings, and the gold from the treasures, and sent them to Hazael, who then went away.
- His own servants made a conspiracy and slew Joash in the house of Millo, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.
